title: Routing fallbacks & prioritization lab notes — May 2027
body:
Context:
This is an interim lab-style note from the routing/fallbacks workstream. Goal: validate a low-latency fallback orchestration policy that can (1) keep tail latency SLOs during regional capacity pressure, (2) respect customer quota priorities, and (3) minimize additional token cost.

Attendees (informal): Aisha, Marcus, Sofia, Jamal, (drop-in: Priya SRE for 20m).

Quick summary:
- Ran two lightweight experiments on the lab cluster (kube-lab-03): soft-fallback v1 (early-roll) and prioritized-fallback v2 (priority buckets + graceful degrade).
- Observed that soft-fallback reduces 99p latency by ~8% on synthetic spiky traffic at the expense of ~2.3% token cost increase due to model variant switching.
- Prioritized-fallback keeps high-priority tenant latency within SLO but increases average latency for low-priority tenants by ~35ms; overall cost delta ~+0.7%.
- Edge-case: requests with pinned model_version ignored fallback path and caused chaotic routing; need pin-aware preflight check.

Experiment details:
- Traffic profile: replicated 'evening spike' from customer-sim generator (burst factor 4x baseline, 60s windows).
- Models involved: rwd-open-7b-q4 (default), rwd-open-7b-q4-fallback (quantized cheaper variant), rwd-13b-medium for high-quality fallback for VIPs.
- Policy configs tested:
  * soft-fallback-v1: router tries primary node pool for 150ms, then routes to compatible model variant in fallback pool.
  * prioritized-fallback-v2: router consults tenant_priority header + quota remaining; high-priority tenants get primary -> larger model fallback if available; low-priority go to quantized pool.

Key metrics (lab numbers):
- Baseline 99p latency: 410ms; baseline cost per 1M tokens: $118.2
- soft-fallback-v1 99p latency: 377ms (−8%), cost: $120.9 (+2.3%)
- prioritized-fallback-v2 high-priority 99p: 392ms; low-priority 99p: 445ms; blended cost: $119.0 (+0.7%)
- Failure mode observed: ~0.6% of requests triggered model-pin bypass leading to queueing on primary = small spike in 95p latency (~30ms).

Notes / interpretation:
- soft-fallback is simplest to implement but increases platform token usage due to more frequent model switching and prefix rewarm. The 2.3% cost is acceptable for many customers if SLOs are critical.
- prioritized-fallback aligns with our product goals (SLA tiers) but introduces fairness tradeoffs; needs clear admin controls and telemetry to show low-priority impact.
- Pin-aware preflight step is required: router must evaluate request.metadata.pinned_model and short-circuit routing decisions or surface a fallback permission flag to the control plane.

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Add pin-aware preflight in router (prototype) — Marcus — ETA: 2027-05-18
- Add telemetry label for fallback-induced model-switching events (trace id + reason) — Sofia — ETA: 2027-05-14
- Run a 24h soak of prioritized-fallback on canary pool with mixed tenants (10% traffic) — Jamal + SRE — ETA: schedule 2027-05-16; results due 2027-05-17
- Draft product note for engineering-facing UI controls for tenant priorities and visibility — Aisha — ETA: 2027-05-20

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we expose per-request fallback preference in the API (opt-in flag) or keep it platform-only? Pros: customer control; Cons: complexity and potential misuse.
- Quota accounting for fallback: when a request falls back to a cheaper model, should quota deduction follow the actual model used or the original requested model? (Current implementation charges based on executed model.)
- Burst vs sustained pressure: lab tests used short spikes. Need longer-duration tests to validate token-cost amortization and KV cache warm-up impacts.

Quick rough design sketch (text):
1) Router receives request -> preflight checks: pinned_model? customer_priority? route_affinity?
2) If primary unavailable within X ms -> consult fallback policy table (tenant priority, remaining_quota, allowed_fallback_variants)
3) Emit telemetry event with fallback_decision, trace->control-plane for visibility and potential override
4) If fallback chosen, use cache-warmup hints (prefix copy / head-of-key fetch) to minimize cold start regressions

Immediate risks:
- Telemetry volume: fallback events could be high-volume; need sampling rules to avoid blowing observability budget.
- Billing disputes: customers might dispute increased token usage if fallbacks are automatic; product/legal alignment needed.

Links referenced / tickets to follow-up:
- PLAT-4122: routing fallback policy table (linked above)
- PR #1864: router preflight hook prototype (linked above)
- Slack thread: #platform-routing "fallback experiments" (internal, see pinned messages 2027-05-11)

Meeting notes (freeform fragments):
- Priya: "If we can surf the KV cache between variants, we might cut rewarm cost in half."
- Marcus: "We should not assume availability of 13b fallback in all regions — add region-compat checks in policy."
- Sofia: "Telemetry needs to include token-delta so product can estimate cost impact per tenant."

Next sync: informal follow-up standup on 2027-05-14 (10:30 PT) to decide canary rollout timing.

Scratchpad TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Add unit test for pinned_model bypass
- [ ] Draft bylaws for quota-charging on fallback
- [ ] Add sample dashboards: fallback-rate by tenant, fallback-cost-delta, pinned-bypass-count

Tagline (for archive search): routing fallback lab — early results, pin-aware preflight required, product decision needed on quota charging.
